why: This is Odd Even Linked List with period 3: walk the list once with a position counter, route nodes at positions 3, 6, 9, ... to a second chain, and append that chain to the first. Both chains keep their order because nodes are appended at the tail.
hints: Each node's destination depends only on its original position mod 3.
Build two chains, 'kept' and 'thirds', each with a head and a tail pointer (or a dummy node), appending every node to one of them.
Link kept's tail to thirds' head and return kept's head. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
pitfalls: Positions count from 1, so the 3rd node (index 2) moves, not the first.
Set the final tail's next to None, otherwise the last kept node may still point into the old list.
Lists shorter than 3 are unchanged; an empty list returns None.
